teaser: The reception thins out by four in the afternoon, and you are the one still refilling the coffee urn, finding chairs for people who have nowhere else to sit. Life path 9 is called the number of letting go, and you are an ISTJ, built to hold things steady rather than release them. That crossing is the center of this reading: a path that asks for an open hand, carried by letters that close around duty instead. The generosity is real. It shows up as casseroles labeled with your name, as folding chairs stacked afterward, as the ride home nobody else thought to arrange. What gets harder is the releasing part — the letting the grief, the person, the cause, actually leave your hands.
excerpt: 'You don't have to fix this,' someone says, at a desk in a night class, after you have already rearranged their schedule to make the course work.
